subject: Agriculture
title: The Dust Bowl
description: A quick, practical guide to The Dust Bowl.

hook.text: In the 1930s, giant dust storms buried farms across the American plains. The sky turned black at noon.

buildup.text: Farmers had plowed up millions of acres of native grassland to plant wheat during a boom market.

discovery.text: When drought hit, there were no roots to hold the soil. Wind carried topsoil hundreds of miles.

twist.text: Dust reached New York City and Washington, D.C. Politicians couldn't ignore what farmers had warned about.

climax.text: 350,000 people fled the plains. Hugh Bennett convinced Congress to create the Soil Conservation Service.

punchline.text: America broke the land. The land broke back.

quiz.question: What caused the Dust Bowl of the 1930s?
options: Plowing native grassland left topsoil exposed to wind during drought
